content: {"findings":[{"file":"index.js","line":168,"severity":"major","message":"The change from `urlObject.pathname.slice(lastIndex, protocolAtIndex)` to `urlObject.pathname.slice(1, protocolAtIndex)` breaks the duplicate-slash removal logic. The `lastIndex` variable tracks the end of the previous protocol match and is still updated each iteration (`lastIndex = protocolAtIndex + protocol.length`), but is no longer used for slicing. This causes two bugs: (1) The first segment incorrectly starts at index 1 instead of 0, dropping the first character of the pathname (typically the leading '/'). (2) For pathnames with multiple protocol-like patterns (e.g., '/path/http://example.com//more'), subsequent segments overlap with previously processed content because they all start from index 1 instead of `lastIndex`, producing duplicated and malformed output."}]}
